newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV ENDS FIRMER ON DOLLAR-BEARISH MARKET.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV ENDS FIRMER ON DOLLAR-BEARISH MARKET.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev advanced to 486-488 per dollar at the close of the local interbank market from 500-503 in the morning because dollar supply outweighed demand throughout the day, dealers said.
"Banks and final clients were offering dollars but there were very few bidders for small volumes, which made sellers constantly lower their asks for the dollar," one dealer said.
Low lev liquidity made some banks and many of their clients sell dollars because they needed levs for salary and tax payments before the end of the month and the year, traders said.
"Expectations of a possible further lev rise also might have been a reason for the low dollar demand and increased supply," another dealer said.
A rise in dollar supply amid dollar-bearish sentiment boosted the lev to 507-510 per dollar at the close on Monday from 522-524 at the opening, dealers said.

The central bank was seen buying dolars near 490 levs today but the volumes were too low to counter the lev rise, traders said. Central bank officials were not available for comment. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
